verdicts.quote: "Authentication across our APIs is done via secure API keys."
verdicts.reason: NMI’s own docs show API key-based auth (Authorization header for REST; security_key for Classic). ([docs.nmi.com](https://docs.nmi.com/reference/authentication?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: "NMI operates exclusively through a partner channel. We don’t directly onboard individual merchants as end users."
verdicts.reason: Access requires joining the partner program or going through a reseller/ISO before credentials are issued, not simple self-serve or generic sales contact. ([nmi.com](https://www.nmi.com/resources/payments-101/faq/?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: "the payment gateway’s real-time v4 API is a complete API that allows you to build any payment features found in your NMI Partner Portal."
verdicts.reason: Vendor says the API covers the full feature set (onboarding, reporting, settings), indicating broad surface area. ([docs.nmi.com](https://docs.nmi.com/reference/nmi-gateway-features?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: "NMI publishes two MCP servers. They do different jobs and most developers connect both."
verdicts.reason: NMI maintains official MCP servers (docs MCP and account-aware MCP), so it’s not “none.” ([docs.nmi.com](https://docs.nmi.com/docs/mcp?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: "NMI operates exclusively through a partner channel."
verdicts.reason: Because meaningful credentials come via partner onboarding (or a reseller), Composio would need partner acceptance/outreach before shipping an integration. ([nmi.com](https://www.nmi.com/resources/payments-101/faq/?utm_source=openai))
